newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CROWD TROUBLE MARS UNITED'S EUROPEAN CUP VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CROWD TROUBLE MARS UNITED'S EUROPEAN CUP VICTORY.

text.p: While Manchester United's supporters were involved in violent scenes with Portugese police on Wednesday, their football team cruised into the semifinals of the European Cup for the first time in 28 years.
Apparently oblivious to the trouble that went on before and after the match, the English champions clinched a semifinal place beating Porto 4-0 on aggregate after the second leg ended 0-0.
United, who weathered some early Porto pressure but who were never in any real danger of losing the tie, will play Borussia Dortmund in one semifinal next month.
Borussia clinched their place with a 1-0 victory over Auxerre for a 4-1 aggregate win. Their goal in the second leg in France was scored by Lars Ricken after 59 minutes.
Holders Juventus clinched their place in the last four with a 2-0 home win over Rosenborg Trondheim of Norway for a 3-1 aggregate victory.
The opening goal was scored by Frenchman Zinedine Zidane in the 29th minute with Nicola Amoruso wrapping it up with an 88th minute penalty.
Juventus will meet Ajax in their semifinal in a repeat of last season's final in Rome which Juventus won 4-2 on penalties after the teams finished 1-1 after extra time.

Ajax, bidding to reach their third successive final, beat Atletico Madrid 3-2 after extra time for a 4-3 aggregate win with the winning goal coming in the last minute of extra time, scored by 23-year-old Nigerian international Tijani Babangida.
If he was the match-winning hero, then goalkeeper Edwin Van Der Sar kept Ajax in the match with a number of superb saves, including one from a second half penalty taken by Juan Esnaider.
Kiko gave Atletico the lead after 29 minutes with Ronald de Boer equalising for the 1995 European champions four minutes after half-time.
Portugese striker Dani then put Ajax ahead eight minutes into extra time only for Milinko Pantic to equalise for the home side with a second penalty seven minutes later.
If the game had finished 2-2 Ajax would have gone through on the away goals rule, but Babangida underlined it for Ajax when he broke through to score the winner.
The semifinals will be played on April 9 and April 23 with the draw in Lausanne on Friday deciding which clubs are at home in the first leg. The final is in Munich on May 28.
